summary: Backend: 25/25 pytest tests pass (meta, auth, listings, customer/seller orders, admin verify/block/unblock, RBAC, exchange rate). Frontend: home, login (3 role buttons + correct redirects), marketplace add-to-cart (badge updates), restaurants (Closed badge for Nile Bakery, modal opens with menu), seller dashboard tabs visible, admin dashboard verify/reject UI all working. CRITICAL bug found: cart is WIPED on page reload due to race condition in CartContext.jsx between load and save useEffects (worsened by React StrictMode double-mount).

ui_bugs.issue: Cart items are wiped from localStorage on hard page reload (F5). The save useEffect writes items=[] to localStorage before the load useEffect's setItems takes effect. In React 18 StrictMode the effects run twice: first run reads saved data, but the save effect overwrites localStorage with empty array; on the second StrictMode mount, the load effect reads the now-empty storage and the cart is permanently empty until the user re-adds items. Verified via test: after adding 2 items localStorage holds them, after page.reload() localStorage becomes {"items":[],...} and UI shows 'Your cart is empty'.

action_items: Fix CartContext.jsx persistence: use lazy useState initializer to read localStorage synchronously, e.g. `const [items, setItems] = useState(() => { try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY))?.items || []; } catch { return []; } });` for items, area, exchangeRate. Then remove the load useEffect entirely. Alternatively add a `loadedRef` and skip the save effect until load completes. Without this fix, refreshing the cart page or any page after adding items deletes the cart.
critical_code_review_comments: CartContext save useEffect runs on initial render with empty state and overwrites a populated localStorage value before the load effect can hydrate state — classic race; under React 18 StrictMode this causes permanent data loss on reload.
server.py login sets cookie with samesite='none' and secure=True which is correct for cross-site preview URL; OK.
server.py /api/orders does not validate that referenced item_id exists in DB — accepts any items payload. Acceptable for demo but worth noting.
No rate limiting / brute force lockout on /api/auth/login (playbook mentions 5-fail lockout). Not implemented; demo-only so low priority.
server.py @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') uses deprecated FastAPI lifecycle (works but should be migrated to lifespan).
seed_data_creation: None — relied on auto-seeded demo data. Tests created TEST_-prefixed shops/products and cleaned up after.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest, 25 tests, all green). The single high-priority issue is cart persistence in /app/frontend/src/context/CartContext.jsx — verify after fix by: login as customer, add items to cart, refresh /cart page, items should remain. Use data-testid 'add-to-cart-{productId}' on Marketplace, 'cart-count-badge' on header, 'place-order-btn' on Cart page. Place-order works only when cart actually has items.
rca of the issue: CartContext.jsx defines two useEffects: (1) load effect with [] deps reads localStorage and calls setItems(saved); (2) save effect with [items,...] deps writes current state to localStorage. Both effects fire after the first render where items=[]. The save effect therefore writes {items:[]} to localStorage, wiping the saved cart. Under React 18 StrictMode (default in CRA dev), the effects double-mount: by the time the second mount's load effect runs, localStorage has already been clobbered to [] and there is nothing to restore. Mitigation: hydrate state synchronously via useState(initFn) or guard the save effect with a `hasLoadedRef` so it does not run before the first load completes.
